title: tolist() does not graph when capture_scalar_outputs = False
bug_description:
repo:
```
@torch.compile(fullgraph=False, backend="eager")
def func(a):
    u0, u1 = a.tolist()
    return a*u0*u1
func(torch.tensor([1,2]))
```


output graph:
```
class GraphModule(torch.nn.Module):
    def forward(self, L_a_: "i64[2][1]cpu"):
        l_a_ = L_a_
        
         # File: /home/lsakka/pytorch/pytorch/example.py:7 in func, code: u0, u1 = a.tolist()
        getitem = l_a_[0]
        item: "Sym(u0)" = getitem.item();  getitem = None
        getitem_1 = l_a_[1]
        item_1: "Sym(u1)" = getitem_1.item();  getitem_1 = None
        
         # File: /home/lsakka/pytorch/pytorch/example.py:8 in func, code: return a*u0*u1
        mul: "i64[2][1]cpu" = l_a_ * item;  l_a_ = item = None
        mul_1: "i64[2][1]cpu" = mul * item_1;  mul = item_1 = None
        return (mul_1,)
        
```
in contrast, the following program does graph break.
```
@torch.compile(fullgraph=False, backend="eager")
def func2(a):
    u0 = a.item()
    return a*u0
```
func2(torch.tensor([1]))



This is problematic because now we have item() in the graphs then we might re-trace 
in autograd and fail because capture_scalar_outputs=False and its too late to know where to graph break!
seen this recently with Ads cc @chauhang @penguinwu @ezyang @bobrenjc93 @pianpwk 

Note that with inductor backend fails to compile !
```
@torch.compile(fullgraph=False, backend="inductor")
def func(a):
    u0, u1 = a.tolist()
    return a*u0*u1
func(torch.tensor([1,2]))
```
a proposed [fix](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/163807) but need to wait for CI and add unit test. 
cc @chauhang @penguinwu @ezyang @bobrenjc93
error_description: tolist() does not cause a graph break when capture_scalar_outputs = False, while item() does. This is problematic because having item() in the graphs can cause re-tracing in autograd to fail when capture_scalar_outputs=False, and it's too late to know where to graph break. With inductor backend, it fails to compile.
